seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [reflection,reflection] show mixed outcomes: no_change x2, pixels,w,x x1, h,pixels,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes: Mirror-axis game rendered on a 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks (board 63x63): bg 9, axis band 10, targets solid 11, reflections 4 holed, pieces 5 holed. A1/A2 move the selection one block row (axis or selected piece), A3/A4 move a selected piece one column (axis = no-op); pieces blocked by board edge and other pieces. A5 cycles axis -> pieces by size desc -> axis. Each piece block off the axis reflects to row 2A-r (ring+hole 4), skipping off-board and piece-occupied dests; holes composite as first solid below else topmost fill (selected piece/axis 0, reflection 4, target shows through as 11). HUD col 63 gains one 11->12 from the top per state-changing action; row 63 static. Unconfirmed: whether the axis itself is ever blocked by pieces (not observed). The target/reflection mixed outcomes in the hypothesis are re-render/re-extraction effects, not click position.
